name: Free plugs on a side
mechanism: The router does not fix a free plug before the search. The search starts from the whole free side at once, so the first leg goes straight to the first corner. The plug is the foot of that leg.
math: Multi-source A*. For each corner c in the strip in front of the free side S, a start link has the cost dist(c, S) + λ · angle(c - foot(c), normal), with foot(c) the projection of c on S, clamped to the inset.
cost: O(k) more start links for each end, with k corners in the strip. Near T_c: 30 ms at 100 nodes, 1 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: minGap between two plugs of a side: 4 to 16, default 8
screen: A scratch run of this note gives the first data: a pure slide of the plug straightens 9% to 13% of the bent ends. Keep the full form when the median of R3 drops by 15% or more on small-clustered and case-dense-groups, with the minimum of R11 at 0.5 or more.

result.note: The option `plugs: side` of the router `corners` is off by default. The median R3 falls 11% to 33% and R4 falls 11% to 31%, with 0 new hard breaks. The bar of 15% on small-clustered and dense-groups is not met. R10 is 0 against 0. The values of `bend` and `most` do not change the records.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on R3, R4 and R11 of the router corners, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. The median R3 falls 11% to 33%, much more than its minimum effect. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 1 of 1 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Plug justification

sources.title: An empirical distribution function for sampling with incomplete information
sources.authors: Ayer, Brunk, Ewing, Reid and Silverman

sources.title: Breaking paragraphs into lines

mechanism: Each plug of a side has an ideal place, where its route wants to leave. The plugs keep their order and a gap of at least s_min. The plugs move the least distance from their ideal places.
math: Minimize Σ (x_i - a_i)^2 with x_(i+1) - x_i ≥ s_min and lo ≤ x_i ≤ hi. Put y_i = x_i - i · s_min: the problem is isotonic regression of a_i - i · s_min. Pool adjacent violators solves it in O(k), then clamp to the side.
cost: O(k log k) for each side with the sort, O(m log m) in total. Less than 1 ms at 100 nodes and 5 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: ideal place: the straight line to the other end, or the first leg of the route
weight of each plug: 1, or the count of its edges
screen: On grid-400 and small-clustered, the minimum of R11 must reach 1.0 on each side with room for its plugs. Drop it when R1 grows by more than 2%.

result.note: The option `plugGap: 6` of the router `corners` raises the R11 minimum on all 6 families, but R11 does not reach 1.0. R1 grows more than 2% on dense-groups, small-clustered and many-groups. The option stays in the code, off by default. The board grid-400 is not in screen-v1.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on R11 and R1 of the router corners, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. R1 grows more than 2% on 3 boards, a loss above the minimum effect. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 1 of 1 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Plug auction

sources.title: The auction algorithm: a distributed relaxation method for the assignment problem

mechanism: Each side has slots at an even spacing. Each end of an edge bids for the slots of its box. The auction gives each end one slot at the lowest total cost, and no two ends share a slot.
math: Assignment problem with c(end, slot) = w_a · angle(slot → other end, normal) + w_d · detour estimate + w_x · crossings of the straight stubs. The auction of Bertsekas with ε-scaling: a bidder raises the price of its best slot by best - second + ε.
cost: O(s · k · log(C / ε)) for each box with k ends and s slots. Less than 2 ms at 100 nodes and 20 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: slots on each side: 2 to 16, or side / s_min
screen: On case-dense-groups and small-clustered, keep it when R1 drops by 5% or more and the minimum of R11 is 1.0, with the q95 of R5 up by less than 3%.

name: Side spill by capacity

sources.title: Register allocation and spilling via graph coloring

mechanism: A side holds at most cap plugs at the spacing s_min. When more ends face that side, the ends with the lowest cost to move spill to the next side. A register allocator spills values in the same way.
math: cap_s = floor(len_s / s_min) - 1. Sort the ends of a full side by the spill cost: the gain of angle to the next side, clockwise or counter-clockwise. Move the cheapest ends until the side fits. Do at most 4 passes around the box.
cost: O(k log k) for each box. Less than 1 ms at 100 and at 1 000 nodes.
params: spill to: the nearer side, or both sides
screen: On mid-fanout (in CI) and a case board with a fan of 20 edges, count the sides with R11 below 1. Keep it when that count drops to 0 and the mean of R10 rises by less than 10°.

name: Angular cohorts share a plug

sources.title: Ckmeans.1d.dp: optimal k-means clustering in one dimension by dynamic programming

mechanism: The ends of a box are sorted by the angle toward their other ends. Breaks in the angle split them into cohorts. Each cohort shares one plug and one short stub, then fans out.
math: Optimal 1D clustering of the angles by dynamic programming: minimize Σ variance within each cohort + β · cohorts. A cohort has 2 or more ends and a spread of θ_max or less.
cost: O(k^2) for each box with k ends. Less than 2 ms at 100 nodes and 20 ms at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On mid-fanout (in CI) and small-clustered, keep it when B1 rises by 0.05 or more and B4 rises by less than 0.02.

result.note: The strategy `stubs` beats `shared` on 1 of the 4 boards, and `ends: source` on 2. The q95 rises above 1 on hub-chain and many-groups, and B1 falls on hub-chain. B2 and R11 rise on all 4 boards. B2 rises 9% to 37% on 3 of them. B4 is worse on all 4 boards. R1 changes by 3% or less, but rises 29% on hub-chain.

strict.note: With the strict rule, stubs-source against shared wins 2 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: `stubs` is at least as good as `shared` on each new win on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `many-groups`. It is better on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `many-groups`. The option `stubs-source` closes a median of 0 of the gap, with the rule `all`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 5 of 5 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Eight-direction plugs
mechanism: A box also gets four corner plugs with diagonal normals. An edge whose direction is near 45° leaves from a corner, so its first leg needs no turn.
math: The set of normals is the 4 side normals and the 4 diagonals. Pick the normal nearest to the direction of the other end. A corner plug sits at the corner, moved in by inset along both sides. Its out point is p + margin · n.
cost: O(1) for each end, as today.
screen: On grid-400 and small-clustered, keep it when the mean of R4 drops by 10% or more and the tight share of R8 does not rise.

name: Groups from routes
mechanism: The router routes each edge with corners first. Two nodes whose routes use the same corridors are similar. A merge on the graph of neighbours joins similar nodes, so each group holds nodes whose edges travel together.
math: Put each route on cells of side 4u. The vector of a node is the count of each cell that its routes touch, with TF-IDF weights. The similarity is the cosine. Average linkage merges only Delaunay neighbours. Cut the merge tree at the ratio r.
cost: One corners route (T_c) and O(n log n) merges. 50 ms at 100 nodes, 1.3 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: weight of the positions: 0 to 1, default 0.5
screen: Against cut on the 10 boards of GRP-R, at the same k: keep it when G2 at the far view is lower on 6 boards or more and Z9 drops.

name: Line breaking on a space-filling curve
method: Analogy: typography (the line breaking of Knuth and Plass)

sources.title: Breaking paragraphs into lines

mechanism: The nodes are sorted along a Hilbert curve. The order breaks into groups as Knuth and Plass break a paragraph into lines. The breaks minimize the cut edges and a badness for groups far from the target size.
math: F(j) = min_i F(i) + out(i, j) + γ · ((j - i - b) / b)^2 over i in [j - 2b, j - b/2]. out(i, j) = deg(i, j) - 2 · inner(i, j), with prefix sums of the degrees and an incremental count of the inner edges. The breaks of level d + 1 are a subset of the breaks of level d, so the levels nest.
cost: O(n · b) for each level. Less than 5 ms at 100 nodes and 50 ms at 1 000 nodes.
screen: Against kd and cut at the same k on the 10 boards of GRP-R: keep it when G2 at the far view is not worse on 8 boards and G6 is above 0.9.

name: A vote of the grouping rules

sources.title: Cluster ensembles: a knowledge reuse framework for combining multiple partitions

mechanism: The rules quadtree, kd, cut and keys make their trees. Each pair of neighbour nodes gets one vote from each rule that puts them in one group. A merge on the votes gives the consensus tree.
math: co(u, v) = (1 / R) Σ_r [group_r(u) = group_r(v)] for Delaunay neighbours, summed over the levels. Average linkage on 1 - co, with merges of neighbours only. Cut at the k of the reference rule.
cost: R trees, O(R · n log n), and the merge. 10 ms at 100 nodes, 100 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: rules: a subset of the registry
screen: Under the seeded moves of MEAS0: keep it when the ARI of G9 is 0.05 or more above the best single rule, with G2 not worse than the median rule.

name: Incumbent bonus for stable groups

sources.title: The stability of hedonic coalition structures
Potential games

mechanism: Each node is a player that picks a neighbour group. Its payoff counts its edges into the group, a cost for the size of the group, and a bonus for its group before an edit. Best responses end in a stable partition.
math: u_v(C) = e(v, C) - λ · abs(C) + β · [C = prev(v)]. This is a symmetric additively separable hedonic game. Its potential Φ = Σ_C Σ_(u<v in C) (a_uv - λ) + β · kept falls at each strict move, so the best responses stop.
cost: O(m) for each sweep, with 3 to 10 sweeps. Less than 5 ms at 100 nodes and 50 ms at 1 000 nodes.
screen: One move of u on 5 seeds of small-clustered and mid-clustered: keep it when the ARI of G9 is 0.95 or more and higher than without the bonus, with G2 up by less than 0.02.

name: Level ladder by line breaking
method: Analogy: typography (the line breaking of Knuth and Plass)

sources.title: Breaking paragraphs into lines

mechanism: A merge tree can give any number of items. A dynamic program picks the item counts of the levels. Each step is near the target ratio, and the far view fits the budget of the host.
math: The candidates are the cut sizes k of the tree. F(k_j) = min_i F(k_i) + (log(k_j / k_i) - log r)^2 + μ · [items + links of k_j > B]. Keep the best path of L levels.
cost: O(K^2 · L) for K candidates. Less than 1 ms.
screen: On nestedGridBoard, case-many-groups and mid-clustered: keep it when the spread of log(lr) of Z5 drops by 30% or more and Z4 is 1 or less at the far view.

name: Coarse links from fine routes

sources.title: Pyramidal parametrics

mechanism: The router routes the edges first. A link of a level then follows the routes of its edges outside its two items. The far view agrees with the near view by its design, as a mipmap comes from its finer image.
math: For the link (A, B), clip each route r_e to the outside of A ∪ B. Take the medoid argmin_e Σ_f F(r_e, r_f), with F the discrete Fréchet distance, over at most 16 sampled routes. Snap its ends to the boundaries of A and B.
cost: O(links · s^2 · p^2) with s sampled routes of p points. 10 ms at 100 nodes, 300 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: pick: the medoid, or the route with the most shared length
screen: On mid-clustered and case-dense-groups: keep it when Z9 drops by 50% or more and the avoidable level through of Z3 does not rise.

name: Budgeted frontier expansion
method: Analogy: auctions and markets (a knapsack of the screen budget)
mechanism: A level is not one depth of the tree. From the root, the step opens the item with the best gain for each new element, until the budget is spent. Large, busy groups open first.
math: Frontier F. gain(c) = the cut edges that opening c shows as its own links, plus w · size(c). cost(c) = children(c) - 1 plus the new links. Greedy by gain / cost with a priority queue. A ladder of budgets gives nested levels, because each frontier refines the last.
cost: O(k log k) for each level. Less than 1 ms.
screen: On mid-clustered and nestedGridBoard: keep it when each level has Z4 of 1 or less and G2 is lower than a fixed depth with the same number of items.

name: Zoom hysteresis
method: Analogy: heating and cooling (the dead band of a thermostat)

sources.title: Feedback systems: an introduction for scientists and engineers

mechanism: pickLevel changes the level at one scale when the reader zooms in, and at a lower scale when the reader zooms out. A small move near a threshold then does not change the view.
math: Level d holds for the scale s in [a_d, b_d]. Go to d + 1 only when s > b_d · (1 + h). Go back to d only when s < b_d · (1 - h).
cost: O(1) for each frame.
screen: A zoom path of 200 steps with 2% noise on case-many-groups: keep it when the level flips drop by 80% or more and Z4 stays at 1.1 or less.

name: Geomorph between levels

sources.title: Progressive meshes

mechanism: Between two levels, each link moves smoothly from its coarse form to the fine routes of its edges. The host draws the blend between two thresholds, so no line jumps.
math: Resample the coarse link L and each fine route r on n points by arc length. At the blend t in [0, 1]: p_i(t) = (1 - t) · L_i + t · r_i. t is a smoothstep of the scale between the two thresholds.
cost: O(m · n) for each frame. 2 ms at 100 nodes and 20 ms at 1 000 nodes, for n = 32.
params: width of the band: 0.1 to 0.5 of the step between two levels
screen: On mid-clustered: keep it when the largest jump between two frames at 1% of zoom apart is less than 2u, and the through count of the blend at t = 0.5 is 0 after a clamp.

name: Bundle level of detail
mechanism: When the lanes of a bundle are less than one pixel apart on the screen, the host draws one stroke. Its width grows with the log of the count. Lanes far enough apart get their own lines.
math: Screen spacing σ = spacing · scale. When σ < σ_min, draw one stroke of width w_0 · (1 + log2(count)). When σ ≥ 2 σ_min, draw the lanes. Blend between the two.
cost: O(bundles) for each frame.
screen: On shared-all over case-many-groups at 5 zoom scales: keep it when the lane legibility count of WILD-060 is 0 and the drawn ink drops.

name: Water-filling room
method: Analogy: typography (the glue of a justified line)

sources.title: Convex optimization
Breaking paragraphs into lines

mechanism: The board can grow by a given share only. Each gap asks for its need. The room goes to the gaps as water fills basins, so the shortfall goes to the gaps where it hurts least.
math: Each gap of boardGaps crosses the board, so the growth of an axis is Σ_g x_g. Minimize Σ_g w_g (d_g - x_g)^2 with Σ_g x_g ≤ W and 0 ≤ x_g ≤ d_g. KKT: x_g = clamp(d_g - ν / (2 w_g), 0, d_g), with ν by bisection and w_g the lanes of the gap.
cost: O(G · log(1 / ε)) for G gaps. Less than 1 ms.
screen: On packedGridBoard, against the maxGrowth curve of ROOM-A: keep it when M4 is lower at the areas 1.25 and 1.40.

name: Room and routes as a market
method: Analogy: auctions and markets (prices that clear a market)

sources.title: Convex optimization

mechanism: A gap sells width at a price. A route pays the price for each lane that it puts through a gap, so routes go around costly gaps. The prices move until the supply of width meets the demand.
math: For t = 1..T: route with the cost len + Σ_g λ_g · [route crosses g]. The excess is x_g = lanes_g · spacing + gutter - width_g. λ_g ← max(0, λ_g + η · (x_g - share_g)). This is dual ascent on area + α · length.
cost: T routes, with T from 3 to 6: 150 ms at 100 nodes, 5 s at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On packedGridBoard: keep it when its points (M1, M4) lie below the curve of ROOM-A, with the q95 of R5 up by less than 5%.

name: Squeeze lanes before opening
mechanism: Before a gap opens, its lanes move closer, down to a floor. The gap opens only for the lanes that do not fit at the floor.
math: s_g = clamp((width_g - gutter) / lanes_g, s_min, spacing). The new need is max(width_g, gutter + lanes_g · s_min).
cost: O(G). Less than 1 ms.
params: scope: each gap, or one value for the board
screen: On packedGridBoard at maxGrowth 0.3: keep it when M1 drops by 10% or more, M4 does not rise, and R12 stays below 0.05.

name: Seam insertion

sources.title: Seam carving for content-aware image resizing

mechanism: The step finds a connected path of cells across the board that goes through the most crowded gaps and through no box. Width goes in along that path only. The step repeats until each gap has its need.
math: Energy e(c) = ∞ in a box and -need(c) in a gap. Vertical seam by dynamic programming: M(i, j) = e(i, j) + min(M(i - 1, j - 1 .. j + 1)). Insert width δ along the seam: each cell right of it moves by δ.
cost: O(cells) for each seam. 50 ms at 100 nodes and 1 s at 1 000 nodes for 20 seams.
params: slope: 1 or 2 cells for each row
screen: On packedGridBoard: keep it when M4 reaches 0 at an area below 1.50 and the count of M2 stays 0.

name: Gusset room
method: Analogy: sewing (a gusset adds cloth in one place)
mechanism: A gap opens only near the place that needs it. The boxes in the shadow of that place move, and the shift fades with the distance along the gap.
math: δ_b = need_g · φ(d_b / R), with d_b the distance of box b along the gap from the place of need and φ(t) = max(0, 1 - t)^2. Then check the order of the boxes on each axis. Where the check fails, open the full line.
cost: O(G · n). 5 ms at 100 nodes, 50 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: fallback: the full line, or no change
screen: On packedGridBoard and nestedGridBoard: keep it when M3 drops by 30% or more at the same M4, and the count of M2 stays 0.

name: Shortest edges first, and other orders
mechanism: The router shared routes the longest edges first, so the short edges join them. The inverse routes the shortest first: short edges stay direct, and long edges join them. An axis of the box tests five orders.
math: Order axis: the longest first (today), the shortest first, by the area of the bounding box, by slack (WILD-023), and 8 random orders with the best one kept. The search is the same discounted A*.
cost: T_c for each order. 8 random orders cost 8 T_c.
params: order: longest, shortest, area, slack, random
screen: On shared and shared-all over case-hub-chain, case-many-groups and small-clustered, with 5 seeds: keep an order when Â12 is 0.64 or more on the q95 of R5 or on B1.

result.note: The inverse order `shortest` loses B1 on 3 of 4 boards (11% to 18% with `shared-all`) and the crossings rise 14% to 50%, except on many-groups. The order `load` is near `span`. The options stay, off by default, and `span` stays the default. The stage follows the canonical NAT-024: the order axis is kept, with `span` as the default.

strict.note: With the strict rule, shared-all-order-shortest against shared-all wins 1 of 4 boards (1 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The option `shared-all-order-shortest` closes a median of 0 of the gap, with the rule `collection`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 2 of 2 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Tight edges first

sources.title: Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies

mechanism: A list scheduler issues first the instructions with the least slack. In the same way, the router routes first the edges with few good ways, and last the edges with many ways of near-equal cost.
math: slack(e) = L2(e) / L1(e) - 1, with L1 the shortest way and L2 the shortest way after a penalty of 3 times on the links of L1. Route in the order of rising slack.
cost: Two more A* searches for each edge: 3 T_c. 90 ms at 100 nodes, 3 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: ties: by id or by length
screen: The same test as WILD-022. Keep it when it beats the best order of WILD-022 on one measure with Â12 of 0.64 or more.

name: Best-response routing game
method: Analogy: game theory (best responses and potential games)

sources.title: Potential games
Equilibrium points in n-person games
How bad is selfish routing?

mechanism: Each edge is a player. In turn, each edge drops its route and takes its best route against the routes of the others. The rounds stop when no edge changes.
math: c_e(r) = L(r) + α · Σ_f X(r, r_f) + β · bends(r). Crossings are symmetric, so Φ = Σ_e (L + β · bends) + α · Σ_(e<f) X is an exact potential. Each strict move lowers Φ, so the rounds end at a Nash equilibrium.
cost: R rounds of T_c with crossing tests, R from 3 to 5. 0.5 s at 100 nodes, 20 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: order of the players: as WILD-022
screen: On case-dense-groups and small-clustered: keep it when R1 drops by 15% or more against corners, with the q95 of R5 up by less than 5%. Give its price of anarchy against WILD-055 on small boards.

name: Angle-priced crossings

sources.title: Drawing graphs with right angle crossings

mechanism: A crossing costs less when it is near a right angle. The router then puts each crossing that it cannot avoid at a steep angle.
math: Link cost len + Σ_x (α_0 + α · (1 - sin θ_x)^p), with θ_x the angle between the link and the leg that it crosses.
cost: One round with crossing tests: 2 T_c. 60 ms at 100 nodes, 2 s at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On case-dense-groups and small-clustered: keep it when the mean of R2 rises by 0.05 or more and R1 does not rise.

name: Queueing price of a gap
method: Analogy: queueing (the delay near the capacity of a server)

sources.title: Urban transportation networks: equilibrium analysis with mathematical programming methods

mechanism: A gap is a server with a capacity of lanes. The cost to put one more lane through a gap rises fast as the gap fills, as the delay of a queue near its capacity.
math: cap_g = floor((width_g - gutter) / spacing). Link cost len · (1 + α · x_g / (cap_g - x_g + 1)), with x_g the lanes already in the gap. Route one by one, or find the equilibrium with Frank-Wolfe steps.
cost: T_c and one gap lookup for each link. 40 ms at 100 nodes, 1.3 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: mode: one by one, or equilibrium
screen: On packedGridBoard with no room: keep it when M4 drops by 30% or more with the q95 of R5 up by less than 10%.

name: Far view first, then refine

sources.title: Near optimal hierarchical path-finding

mechanism: The router routes the links of the far view first. Each finer edge then searches only a corridor around the link of its two far items. Coarse and fine agree, and the search is smaller.
math: Corridor C_e = the boxes of the items along the coarse link, made larger by w. A* on the corners in C_e only. When no way exists, A* on the full graph.
cost: The level links and T_c times the share of the corridor, near 0.3 T_c to 0.6 T_c. 20 ms at 100 nodes, 0.5 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: level of the corridor: far view, or the coarsest level that splits the ends
screen: On mid-clustered (in CI) and small-clustered: keep it when Z9 drops by 30% and the time drops, with the q95 of R5 up by less than 5%.

name: Candidate routes and a joint choice

sources.title: Finding the k shortest loopless paths in a network

mechanism: Each edge gets k candidate routes that pass the boxes on different sides. A local search picks one candidate for each edge, to lower the crossings and the length together.
math: Candidates: the k shortest loopless ways of Yen on the corner graph, one for each class of the boxes passed on the left. A table X[e, i][f, j] of crossings, pruned by bounding boxes. Minimize Σ L + α Σ X with simulated annealing or tabu search.
cost: k T_c for the candidates and O(k^2 m^2) for the table before the pruning. 1 s at 100 nodes. Too slow above 1 000 nodes without more pruning.
screen: On the 3 case boards: keep it when R1 drops by 20% or more against corners, at a time below 10 T_c.

name: Route each group alone, then stitch

sources.title: Near optimal hierarchical path-finding

mechanism: The router routes the edges inside each group of the tree alone. An edge between groups goes through portals on the borders of the groups. A small graph of portals joins the groups, as in HPA*.
math: Portals: one entry point for each free span of a shared border. The abstract graph holds the cached shortest ways between the portals of each group. A* on the abstract graph, then refine each abstract link inside its group.
cost: Σ T_c(group) and the abstract search: near linear. 30 ms at 1 000 nodes, near 1 s at 10 000 nodes (estimates).
params: smooth the result: on or off
screen: On mid-clustered (in CI): keep it when the time drops by 3 times or more against corners, with the median of R5 up by less than 2%.

name: Detect highways after routing
mechanism: Each edge routes alone. Then the step finds the stretches where several routes run near each other, and makes each stretch a highway with its lanes. The trigger is the overlap, not a key.
math: Sample each route each u / 2, and put the samples in cells of side w. A stretch is a longest sequence of cells that the same set S of routes crosses in order, with abs(S) ≥ 2 and a length of L_min or more. The spine is the mean of the samples of S. The lanes snap to it.
cost: O(samples · log) after T_c. 40 ms at 100 nodes, 1.3 s at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On small-clustered and case-many-groups: keep it when B1 is 0.10 or more, B4 is below 0.1 and R9 is 0.

name: Approval corridors
method: Analogy: voting (approval voting) and set cover

sources.title: Approval voting
A greedy heuristic for the set-covering problem

mechanism: Each edge approves each link that lies on a way within 1 + ε of its shortest. A greedy cover picks few links that serve the most edges. The edges then route on the picked links at a discount.
math: Approve (i, j) when d_s(i) + w_ij + d_t(j) ≤ (1 + ε) · d*_e, from one forward and one backward search for each edge. Score of a link = its approvals. Pick the top links until each edge has an approved way in the set. Then discounted A*, as in shared.
cost: Two full searches for each edge: 2 T_c to 3 T_c. 100 ms at 100 nodes, 3 s at 1 000 nodes.
screen: Against shared-all on case-many-groups and small-clustered: keep it when B1 rises with the q95 of B3 at 1 + ε or less.

name: Warrant highways from the demand matrix

sources.title: Urban transportation networks: equilibrium analysis with mathematical programming methods

mechanism: The step counts the edges between each pair of groups at a level, as a survey of trips. A pair with demand over a warrant gets a highway between the hubs of its groups. Light pairs go direct.
math: OD_d(A, B) = the edges between the items A and B of level d. A highway when OD ≥ τ and span(A, B) ≥ L_min. An edge of the pair goes plug, hub of A, spine, hub of B, plug. d is the coarsest level that splits the pair.
cost: O(m) for the matrix, and T_c for the spines and the legs. Near the cost of sections.
screen: Against sections on case-hub-chain and small-clustered: keep it when B1 is within 0.02 and R7 is lower.

result.note: The screen of EDA-033. The strategy `od-cells` beats `shared` on 2 of the 4 boards (hub-chain, many-groups), alone and with the gate `stretch`. Its q95 is 1.000 on each board, but B1 is 0.073 and 0.104 on small-clustered and dense-groups, against 0.210 and 0.307. The level 1 wins on 0 boards and the level 3 bundles almost nothing. The screen of the step `highway` has no measure of Z9 or B8. The strategy stays in the registry.

strict.note: With the strict rule, od-cells against shared wins 2 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: `od-cells` is at least as good as `shared` on each new win on no board. Z9 has no value, because the results of `follow` have no levels. `shared` has 0 runs on `hub-chain` and `many-groups`, so a new run is worse on B8 runs there. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 5 of 5 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Savings merge with a fair share
method: Analogy: economics of shared roads (cost sharing)

sources.title: Scheduling of vehicles from a central depot to a number of delivery points

mechanism: Each edge starts alone. The two bundles whose merge saves the most ink merge first. A merge holds only when each edge pays less than alone: its share of the shared ink plus its own detour.
math: s(A, B) = ink(A) + ink(B) - ink(A ∪ B), with the ink of a trunk to the split point. Accept when for each e: shared / abs(A ∪ B) + own(e) + detour(e) ≤ alone(e). A priority queue of the savings over pairs of near bundles.
cost: O(p log p) merges for p candidate pairs, each with a trunk test. 50 ms at 100 nodes, 2 s at 1 000 nodes.
screen: Against trunks on mid-fanout (in CI) and small-clustered: keep it when B1 rises with the q95 of B3 at 1.2 or less.

name: Highways from the level links
mechanism: The router routes the links of the far view first. Each edge between two far items follows the link of its items as its highway, and its lanes stack along the link.
math: For e = (u, v): d* = the coarsest level where u and v are in different items A and B. The way: plug of u, the start of link_d*(A, B) through A, the link, the end of the link, plug of v. Inside an item, the same rule repeats on the finer level.
cost: The level links of today and two short A* searches for each edge: near 0.5 T_c. 20 ms at 100 nodes, 0.6 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: repeat inside the items: on or off
screen: On mid-clustered (in CI) and case-dense-groups: keep it when Z9 is 0, B1 is at least the value of sections, and R7 is not higher.

result.note: The strategy `level-links` beats `shared` on 1 of the 4 boards. B1 rises 154% on hub-chain and 293% on many-groups, and R1 falls 48% to 53% there. But the q95 rises 5% and 15%, and B6 is 180 degrees. The screen of the step `highway` has no level measure, so Z9 and B8 are not measured.

strict.note: With the strict rule, level-links against shared wins 1 of 4 boards (1 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: `level-links` is at least as good as `shared` on each new win on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`. It is better on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`. Z9 has no value, because the results of `follow` have no levels. `shared` has 0 runs on `hub-chain` and `many-groups`, so a new run is worse on B8 runs there. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 4 of 4 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Streets along the cuts
method: Analogy: city blocks and the seams of a garment
mechanism: A guillotine grouping cuts the board with lines. The free parts of those lines become streets. Each edge between groups goes to the nearest street and travels along the streets.
math: The street graph: the cut lines of cut or kd, cut to their free parts, with nodes at their crossings. Each edge: A* to the nearest street point on the border of its group, A* on the street graph, then A* down. Lanes on each street in bundle order.
cost: O(n) street segments. T_c on a smaller graph. 30 ms at 100 nodes, 1 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: cost to reach a street: 0 to 4 u
screen: On nestedGridBoard and case-many-groups: keep it when B7 and R1 drop, with the q95 of R5 at 1.6 or less.

name: Manifolds for a fan to a row
mechanism: When one node links to many boxes in a row, one header line goes along the row, in the gap before it. A short tap leaves the header at a right angle to each box.
math: Find the targets of u whose centers lie in one band on an axis, with 1D clustering, k_min or more. The header lies on the free line in the gap before the row, from the first tap to the last. The feed goes from u to the start of the header by A*.
cost: O(m log m) and T_c of the feeds. 5 ms at 100 nodes, 100 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: side of the taps: near or far
screen: On mid-fanout (in CI) and a small case board with fans: keep it when B1 rises by 0.1 or more and the mean of R3 drops.

name: Conservative coalescing of near routes

sources.title: Improvements to graph coloring register allocation
Iterated register coalescing

mechanism: Two routes that go parallel and close become one corridor, as a compiler merges two copies of one value. The merge is conservative: it adds no crossing and no route through a box.
math: A candidate pair: legs within 5° and a distance d or less, with an overlap of L or more. The merge moves both legs to their mean line. Accept when crossings(after) ≤ crossings(before), through = 0 and the detour is under its cap. Repeat to a fixed point, cheapest first.
cost: O(m log m) with a grid of segments. 5 ms at 100 nodes, 100 ms at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On corners over small-clustered: keep it when B1 is 0.05 or more, R1 does not rise, and R9 is 0.

result.note: The strategy `zipper` beats `shared` on 2 of the 4 boards, and `adhesion: 1` also on 2. It fails only on the q95, by 0.1% to 1.5%. Against `shared-ways`, B1 rises 12% to 199% on all 4 boards, B2 rises, and R1 falls on 3 boards. B6 and R4 rise. The screen has no measure of B7 or R12. A stretch gate can make it pass. The strategy stays in the registry.

strict.note: WILD-037 is screened with NAT-022 as the strategy zipper. With the strict rule, zipper-a1 against shared wins 3 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule). But on hub-chain, B4 rises from 0.063 to 0.316 and R1 from 68 to 80, and the screen field of the record forbids that rise. Thus the guard keeps the record dropped. Strict count 3, kept dropped by the guard.

rescreen.note: `zipper` is at least as good as `shared` on each new win on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. It is better on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 6 of 6 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

name: Braid crossings at the best place

sources.title: Theory of braids

mechanism: The order of the lanes at the entry and at the exit of a highway fixes the crossings that it needs. The step writes the change as a braid of swaps, and does each swap where the highway is long and straight.
math: Needed crossings = inv(π_in, π_out), the count of inversions, in O(k log k). It is a lower bound of B5 on this highway. Write the swaps as a bubble-sort word. A dynamic program gives each swap to a segment with the lowest 1 / len + λ · curvature.
cost: O(k^2 + segments · k) for each highway. Less than 5 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: place: the longest segment, or the ends
screen: On shared-all over case-many-groups: keep it when B5 equals the lower bound on 90% of the highways and the body crossings sit on the straightest segments.

name: One global lane order

sources.title: Line crossing minimization on metro maps
Edge routing with ordered bundles

mechanism: Today each run, or each stretch of a bundle, orders its lanes. The inverse fixes one order of all the edges, and every run uses it. Two edges then keep one side of each other everywhere.
math: Key of e: the rank of its source along a Hilbert curve, then the rank of its target. Or sifting: move one edge at a time to its best place in π, with incremental counts of the crossings of the runs.
cost: O(m log m) for the key. O(m^2) for sifting, with a cap at 2 000 edges.
screen: Against the order bundle on shared-all over case-many-groups: keep it when the end crossings drop below 687, with 0 body crossings.

name: Flush lanes after an exit
method: Analogy: heating and cooling (a reducing duct)
mechanism: When a lane leaves a highway, the other lanes can stay straight. A dynamic program picks the side to which the lane stack is flush on each segment, so the lanes that go on do not shift.
math: The state is the offset o_j of the stack on segment j: flush left, flush right, centered, or a lane index. Cost = Σ abs(Δ lateral place) of the lanes that go on, plus μ for each exit on the inner side. O(J · S^2) for J segments and S states.
cost: O(J · S^2) for each highway. Less than 1 ms.
screen: On trunks over case-dense-groups and shared-all over case-many-groups: keep it when the sum of the lateral shifts drops by 50% and the maximum of C2 does not rise.

name: Lane changes as voice leading

sources.title: The geometry of musical chords

mechanism: When a lane must shift to the side, it glides over a length that grows with the shift. A voice moves to the nearest note of the next chord in the same way. The slots of each next run keep the total shift small.
math: Match the lanes to the slots of run j + 1 by min Σ abs(pos_j(e) - pos_(j+1)(e)). In 1D, the sorted match is optimal, in O(k log k). A shift Δ becomes a quintic S curve over the length max(ℓ_0, c · abs(Δ)).
cost: O(k log k) for each joint. Less than 1 ms.
screen: On shared-all over case-many-groups: keep it when the maximum of C2 on the lane shifts drops by 50% and B5 does not rise.

name: Right-angle crossing nudge

sources.title: Drawing graphs with right angle crossings

mechanism: Near each crossing of two curves, both curves turn so they cross at a steeper angle. A short straight piece through the crossing keeps the angle, and the curves blend back inside the free space.
math: At a crossing x with angle θ < θ_min: turn each tangent by (θ_min - θ) / 2 about x over a window w. Put a cubic with the new tangent at x and G1 joints at the ends of the window. Reject the change when the clearance falls below the margin.
cost: O(X · w) for X crossings. 10 ms at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On case-dense-groups with the curve smooth: keep it when the minimum of R2 rises by 15° and C7 stays 0.

name: Optical lane spacing at bends
mechanism: Two lanes look closer on a tight bend than on a straight leg at the same spacing. The spacing grows a little where the curvature is high, so the lanes look even.
math: s(p) = s_0 · (1 + k · s_0 · abs(κ(p))), with a cap at 1.5 s_0. The offsets of highwayCurves use s(p) on each arc.
cost: O(lanes · arcs). Less than 1 ms.
screen: Keep it only when R12 on the curves drops and the bends that need room (HWC-D) do not rise. A study with readers decides the final value of k.

name: Curve for each edge by a small portfolio
mechanism: Each route tries the curve types arc, smooth, clothoid and spline. A score of the curve measures picks the best type for that route.
math: score(c) = Σ_i w_i · norm(C_i(c)) over C2, C3, C7 and C8. Take the type with the lowest score. A tie goes to the cheaper type.
cost: Four times the curve step. Less than 10 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: types: a subset of the registry
screen: On case-dense-groups and small-clustered: keep it when the median score beats the best single type by 5%, with less than 30% of the routes in a second style.

name: A portfolio for each board

sources.title: The algorithm selection problem
SATzilla: portfolio-based algorithm selection for SAT

mechanism: For one board, the pipeline tries a short list of complete settings: group, router, curve and room. The suite measures each, and the pipeline keeps the best weighted score within a time budget.
math: score(s) = Σ_i w_i · rank-normalized measure_i(s). Keep the setting with the lowest score, and the Pareto set to show. Stop a setting when its time passes the budget.
cost: The sum of the times of the settings. CI for the full list.
screen: On the boards of SCREEN: keep it when its score beats the best single setting on 60% of the boards.

name: Learned choice of the strategy

sources.title: The algorithm selection problem
SATzilla: portfolio-based algorithm selection for SAT
What would a graph look like in this layout? A machine learning approach to large graph visualization

mechanism: Features of the board predict the best setting, so only one setting routes. A model trained on the records of SCREEN maps the features to the winner of WILD-045.
math: Features: n, m, m / n, degree skew, the coefficient of variation of the box sizes, the nearest-neighbour ratio of the centers, the share of edges with keys, the largest fan-out and the mean span over u. Model: k nearest neighbours or gradient-boosted trees.
cost: Features in O(n log n). The training is offline.
screen: Leave one family out: keep it when the chosen setting is within 5% of the portfolio score on 70% of the boards.

name: Automatic tuning with successive halving

sources.title: Hyperband: a novel bandit-based approach to hyperparameter optimization
sources.authors: Li, Jamieson, DeSalvo, Rostamizadeh and Talwalkar

sources.title: The irace package: iterated racing for automatic algorithm configuration
sources.authors: López-Ibáñez, Dubois-Lacoste, Pérez Cáceres, Birattari and Stützle

mechanism: TUNE sweeps the options. Successive halving makes it cheap: many settings try small boards, the best part goes on to larger boards, and only a few reach the largest.
math: Hyperband with the budgets 100, 400 and 1 000 nodes. Sample n_0 settings from each schema. Keep the top 1 / η at each rung by the weighted score, and compare with Â12.
cost: Near η · log_η(R) times one full sweep of the best few. CI only.
screen: Tune on seeds 1 to 3 and test on seeds 4 and 5: keep it when the tuned setting beats the defaults with Â12 of 0.64 or more on the test seeds.

name: Tune on crops of the board
mechanism: A large board is costly to tune. The tuner cuts a few windows of 100 to 200 nodes from it and tunes on the windows. The whole board then uses the best setting.
math: k random squares that hold n_w nodes each. An edge cut by the border goes to a fixed point on the border. Rank the settings on the windows. The Kendall tau between the window ranks and the full ranks checks the proxy.
cost: k windows times the settings times T_c(n_w).
screen: On mid-clustered (in CI): keep it when the Kendall tau between the window ranks and the full ranks is 0.7 or more over 10 settings.

name: Room and routes to a fixed point
mechanism: The pipeline routes, opens the room that the routes need, and routes again on the opened board. It stops when the routes and the gaps stop changing, or after three rounds.
math: x_(t+1) = Room(Route(x_t)). Stop when the largest change of a gap is below u / 2, or at t = 3. When it oscillates, damp it: x_(t+1) = x_t + 0.5 · (Room - x_t).
cost: Three times T_c and the room step. 100 ms at 100 nodes, 3 s at 1 000 nodes.
screen: On packedGridBoard: keep it when M4 is 0 at a lower M1 than one pass of ROOM.

name: Incremental routing after a move

sources.title: Difference metrics for interactive orthogonal graph drawing algorithms

mechanism: When one box moves, only the routes near it change. The routes that touch the old or the new place of the box, or end at it, route again. The others keep their points.
math: Dirty region D = inflate(box_old ∪ box_new, margin). Route e again when its route meets D or one of its ends is the moved box. Check the other routes against the new obstacles, and route again each one that fails.
cost: O(dirty · A*) for each move. 1 to 5 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: repair: route again, or shift the points
screen: Under the seeded moves of MEAS0 on small-clustered and mid-clustered: keep it when the mean of Z10 drops by 50% and R1 and R5 stay within 2% of a full route.

name: Advice to the layout
mechanism: The router gives the host a push for each box: the direction that makes the routes around the box shorter. The later joint step of placement and routing can use the push as a force.
math: f_b = Σ_e the push of each route that bends at a corner of b: the unit vector from the corner toward the chord without that bend, times the excess length. Divide by the size of the box.
cost: O(Σ points of the routes). Less than 5 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: cap of a push: 0.5 to 4 u
screen: On small-clustered, move each box by 0.5u along its push and route again: keep it when the median of R5 drops by 3% or more with no overlap of boxes.

name: An anytime pipeline

sources.title: Using anytime algorithms in intelligent systems

mechanism: The pipeline gives a usable picture at once and better pictures later. Straight lines come first, then corner routes, then highways and curves. The host shows the latest complete stage.
math: Stages S_0..S_k with the times t_i. At the deadline τ, show S_j with the largest j where Σ_(i≤j) t_i ≤ τ. Each stage keeps the plugs of the stage before it, so the picture changes little.
cost: The sum of the stages. The first picture costs O(m).
screen: On mid-clustered (in CI): keep it when the first picture comes in less than 50 ms and Z10 between the last two stages is below 2u.

name: Input in any order
mechanism: Today the order of the edges in the input can change the routes. The routers sort the edges by a stable hash of their ids first. The same board in any order then gives the same routes.
math: Order = sort by (rule key, hash64(edge.id)). The test shuffles the input k times and compares the routes by the Fréchet distance.
cost: O(m log m). Less than 1 ms.
screen: Shuffle small-clustered 10 times: keep it when each route is equal over the shuffles, against the spread of today.

result.note: The values are medians by router over the 14 inputs, with 20 shuffles. The built-in routers already sort the edges by their ids, so the stable order gives the same routes. All 126 pairs have the same measures and hard counts. stableOrderStrategy stays as a tool for other routers.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on the routes over the shuffles, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. The stable order gives the same routes, so each board is a tie. The old rule counted the ties as wins. The verdict does not change.

name: An ink floor from moats

sources.title: When trees collide: an approximation algorithm for the generalized Steiner problem on networks

mechanism: Bundles save ink, but the largest possible saving is not known. A primal-dual bound of the Steiner forest gives a floor for the ink of each drawing that joins the same plug pairs. B1 then has a ceiling.
math: Grow moats around the plugs of the pairs that are not yet joined, at one rate. The sum of the growth of the active moats is a dual value LB ≤ OPT. Then inkSaved ≤ 1 - LB / Σ L(r_e). Boxes make OPT larger, so the bound holds.
cost: O(p^2 log p) for p plugs. Up to 2 000 plugs in less than 1 s.
screen: A test: the bound is at most the ink of each router on each board. Then the bench gives B1 / B1_max on 5 boards.

name: Exact answers on small boards

sources.title: Finding the k shortest loopless paths in a network
Parallelizing the dual revised simplex method

mechanism: On boards with up to 12 edges, an exact solver picks one route for each edge from k candidates. It finds the fewest crossings and the shortest length. Each router gets its gap to this answer for MEAS2.
math: Candidates: Yen with k = 6. ILP: x_ei in {0, 1}, Σ_i x_ei = 1, y_eifj ≥ x_ei + x_fj - 1. Minimize Σ L_ei x_ei + α Σ X_eifj y_eifj. HiGHS, or branch and bound with the bound Σ_e min_i L_ei.
cost: Seconds for 12 edges. CI only.
screen: It must find the optimum of a brute force on 20 boards with 6 edges. The optimum is over the candidates only, so the note gives it as an upper bound of the true optimum.

name: Order fragility and the price of anarchy

sources.title: How bad is selfish routing?

mechanism: The bench routes a board with 20 random orders of the edges. The spread of each measure is its order fragility. The ratio of the default order to the best of the 20 shows what a better order can gain.
math: frag_f = IQR(f over the orders) / median(f). poa_f = f(default) / min(f over the orders).
cost: 20 T_c. CI only above 400 nodes.
screen: On shared and sections over 3 boards: keep the measure when two routers differ in fragility by 2 times or more.

result.note: The values are the medians of route.order.crossings by router over the 14 inputs, with 20 shuffles. The fragility is 0 for each router and each input, and changed is 0. No two routers differ by 2 times, so the measure does not rank them. W3 stays as a check of the screen (--shuffles).

strict.note: This record screens a measure, not a strategy. The screen field of the record decides on the fragility of the routers, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. The verdict does not change.

name: Tracing load

sources.title: Cognitive measurements of graph aesthetics

mechanism: A reader traces one edge from end to end. Each crossing, merge and split on the way is a place to choose. The measure counts these places for each edge, with a weight for how hard each one is.
math: T(e) = crossings + 2 · (merges and splits where e is not the outer lane) + 0.5 · bends. Report q_0.5 and q_0.95.
cost: O(n log n) with the pass of R1.
screen: Rank the 9 routers on 3 boards: keep the measure when its ranks differ from the ranks of R1, with a Kendall tau below 0.8.

name: Ink hot spots
mechanism: B7 counts the cells that the ink touches. A hot spot is a small area with much ink. The measure gives the 95th percentile of the ink in each cell, against the straight lines.
math: h = q_0.95(ink in each cell of side 4u) / q_0.95(ink of the straight lines in each cell).
cost: O(n log n).
screen: Keep the measure when it separates the routers with bundles from the routers without bundles on 3 boards, where B7 does not.

name: Monotone share

sources.title: Monotone drawings of graphs
sources.authors: Angelini, Colasante, Di Battista, Frati and Patrignani

mechanism: A route that goes toward its target on both axes all the way is easy to follow. The measure gives the share of the routes that are monotone in the direction from the source to the target.
math: mono(e) = 1 when each leg outside the plug stubs has dx · sign(Δx) ≥ -ε and dy · sign(Δy) ≥ -ε. Report the share.
cost: O(points).
screen: Keep the measure when its Spearman correlation with R7 over the routers and the boards is below 0.8.

name: Lane legibility at each zoom
mechanism: A lane helps only when the reader can tell it from its neighbour. At the scale of each level, the measure counts the bundles whose lanes are less than one pixel apart.
math: leg_d = share of the runs of level d with spacing · scale_d < 1 px, with scale_d from pickLevel.
cost: O(runs) for each level.
screen: Keep the measure when it is above 0 for some routers at some levels on case-many-groups.
